topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture objectives, historical context of cancer hallmarks, and the overarching theme of growth control loss.

topics.label: Deregulated growth and proliferative signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive continuous proliferative and survival signaling.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in hematological and epithelial cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how oncogenic alterations prevent maturing progenitor cells from completing normal lineage differentiation.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis, replicative limits, and p53 stress safeguards
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the mechanisms cancer cells use to disable intrinsic tumor-suppressive fail-safes such as programmed cell death, telomere-driven senescence, and p53 surveillance.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolite signaling in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how cancer cells alter metabolic pathways toward aerobic glycolysis and utilize oncometabolites to drive epigenetic and transcriptional changes.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and the angiogenic switch
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the induction of new blood vessel growth necessary to sustain tumor survival and expansion beyond diffusion limits.

topics.label: Metastatic invasion, dissemination, and clonal genetics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the multi-step cascade of metastatic dissemination, clinical monitoring methods, colonization constraints, and the genetic features of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Concluding summary and lecture wrap-up
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic synthesizes the core themes of the lecture on hallmark convergence and provides final administrative remarks.
